chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Umar ibn Yazid that Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
Seek nearness to God Almighty by sympathizing with your brethren.
ai.seo_question: How can one achieve nearness to God through social interaction?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this concise directive from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking social ethics directly to spiritual elevation, emphasizing that *muwasat* (sharing in needs or sympathy) is not merely a social courtesy but a means of *qurb* (nearness) to God. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of worship and social conduct, where caring for the community is viewed as an act of devotion. The instruction underscores the communal responsibility of believers to support one another, reinforcing the idea that spiritual proximity is achieved through tangible acts of solidarity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-26 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Umar ibn Yazid that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
Seek nearness to God by sympathizing with your brethren.”
